text_summary.body: The province's people who returned from the captivity, each to his town, with eleven named leaders headed by Zerubbabel and Jeshua; the families and townspeople, four priestly houses (4,289), 74 Levites, 128 singers, 139 gatekeepers and 392 temple servants and descendants of Solomon's servants; 652 who could not prove their descent and priests excluded pending Urim and Thummim; a total of 42,360 with 7,337 servants and 200 singers, 736 horses, 245 mules, 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys; gifts of 61,000 darics, 5,000 minas of silver and 100 priests' garments.

setting.period: 538 BC onward (Ezra's framework); possibly a composite list
setting.body: Ezra 1:11 ends with Sheshbazzar bringing the vessels "when the captives were brought up"; Ezra 2 follows with the list. 1 Esdras 5:1–6 places this list after Zerubbabel's contest before Darius, in Darius's second year. Ryle suggests that Zerubbabel may have led a second contingent; Batten finds features (qāhāl; the gifts) suggesting a date later than Cyrus.

constraints.textual_assertion: Now these are the children of the province who went up out of the captivity
assumptions: Ezra places the return after Cyrus's decree (1:1–11); 1 Esd 5:1–6 places it under Darius — that reading is recorded as disputed and not modelled.

terminology.gloss: A Persian title for the governor (Adeney via Guzik); in Neh 8:9 applied to Nehemiah.
Persian gold coins (Ryle); Batten notes that some connect the word with the Greek drachma. Whether the name derives from Darius is "far from certain" (Ryle).

competing_reconstructions.label: The first return under Cyrus (538/537), led by Zerubbabel and Jeshua
competing_reconstructions.summary: The list records those who came up after Cyrus's decree.

competing_reconstructions.label: A return (or the list) dated to Darius I's reign
proponents: L. W. Batten (1913): features later than Cyrus
competing_reconstructions.summary: 1 Esdras sends Zorobabel up under Darius; Batten reads the list as reflecting a later, organised community.

competing_reconstructions.label: Two returns: Sheshbazzar's, then Zerubbabel's second contingent
competing_reconstructions.summary: Sheshbazzar's position may have been temporary; Zerubbabel arrived later as resident governor.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik takes the list as the first wave of repatriation, treats Zerubbabel and Sheshbazzar as probably the same person, and quotes Kidner on the three different itemised totals.

open_questions: Whether Sheshbazzar and Zerubbabel are the same person (under review on the vessels record).
Population of post-exilic Judah: estimates range from 20,000 (Albright) to 235,000 (Schultz) (Yamauchi via Guzik; not verified).
